observed_anchor: Current main exposes only linux.process.spawn.v0::(Int)->Int to canonical process hostcalls; current workspace selects shared Bytes/Buffer plus String/argv/effect signatures as the next discriminator.
source_implication: POSIX process argv is an array of pointers to null-terminated character strings, while a typed component model independently distinguishes Unicode string from list<u8>/byte buffer. This supports keeping Clay String/argv semantics distinct from arbitrary byte transport.
hypothesis: A canonical Clay interface should preserve arbitrary non-NUL octets in a Bytes/Buffer carrier while treating process argv as a distinct string-vector surface with explicit NUL rejection and effect signatures.
strongest_counterhypothesis: A host-native bytes argv representation could make a separate Unicode String surface unnecessary for Linux-only v0.1 semantics; premature generalization could add type surface without improving the canonical VM path.

discriminating_experiment.name: NUL_INVALID_UTF8_HOST_BOUNDARY
discriminating_experiment.promotion_limit: This establishes host-boundary semantics only; it is not evidence that ClayVM/TypedIR already implements Bytes, argv, or String process transport.
